set.story: Totem poles are tall carved wooden poles made by Indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest coast of North America. The phrase was in use by the late 1930s and was made famous by H. Allen Smith's 1941 humor book Low Man on a Totem Pole; it assumes the top figure is most important, but many Native carvers did not rank figures that way, and some put the most important at the bottom.

why: 'common by the 1930s' overstates: earliest known uses are 1939-1941; spread by the 1941 H. Allen Smith book
